tagline: Along the Canadian line from the St. Lawrence to Lake Champlain.
intro: Out of Massena near the St. Lawrence, the road runs east never far from the Canadian line, through Hogansburg and Fort Covington to Malone, then on by Chateaugay, Ellenburg and Mooers to Rouses Point on Lake Champlain, 84 miles of rural corridor with roadside farm stands.

For years the military used it to move troops and equipment between the two waters. Fort Covington was French Mills until 1817, when it took the name of a general mortally wounded in the War of 1812, four years after a blockhouse went up there to shelter wounded soldiers.

moments.title: Wilder Homestead
moments.text: Near Malone stands the 1843 Greek Revival farmhouse where Almanzo Wilder grew up, the boyhood that Laura Ingalls Wilder wrote into Farmer Boy.

moments.title: Chateaugay
moments.text: The Chateaugay River runs north through the town toward the St. Lawrence, the regional byway brochure points travelers to its 120-foot High Falls, and the village has come through three great fires.

moments.title: Rouses Point
moments.text: A first fort here was abandoned when a new survey put it in Canada, the locals carried off its stone for their own houses, and it became known as Fort Blunder.

sources.label: Adirondack Regional Tourism Council, Adirondack North Country Scenic Byways (p. 10)
